claims.text: The governing distance measurement is the GPS trace, not the rounded trip-record copy. EV-GPS-00502 records trace_distance_km of 8.77 km between the recorded pickup event and the recorded dropoff event against a booked optimal of 5.6 km on EV-TRIP-00502 — an excess of 3.17 km, which is 56.6% of the optimal route and far above the 0.8 km absolute floor. Both establishment tests in POL-RD-01 therefore pass on this trip's own evidence. I rely on the trace figure and expressly do not use trip_record.actual_distance_km (8.8 km), which is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and may not be cited for the threshold test.

The excess also clears the materiality gate in POL-RD-01. An excess above 50% of optimal_distance_km is additionally a MATERIAL deviation, and 56.6% is above that line; the alternative 8.0 km absolute limb is not needed. Materiality is assessed on the excess remaining after any POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05 or POL-RD-12 adjustment, and for the reasons set out below no such adjustment survives on this record. This is a MATERIAL deviation, so the driver-profile check in POL-RD-06 is mandatory.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. The artifacts describe the same trip — trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-00502, and the trace's first fix at 2026-08-21T20:46:40+08:00 matches trip_record.started_at — and the excess is measured from an unimpaired trace (100% coverage, 145 fixes, no gaps, max gap 0.0 s, 10 s sampling). The burden has now shifted to the driver, who must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause to invoke an exculpatory provision; an assertion that cites no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded. The rider's own profile does not aggravate the claim: deviation_claims_60d is 0, so the additional-corroboration rule for serial claimants is not engaged.

No closure or traffic-advisory exoneration is available under POL-RD-03, and I disclose the impairment of the artifact I rely on rather than presenting it as clean: EV-ADVIS-00502-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0, and its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT — no advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window. POL-RD-03(a) requires an advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses; there is none, and the driver's reference in his statement to a 'road works sign near Telok Blangah' does not name a road appearing anywhere in this record and identifies no advisory ID. The absence is itself citable, and on it the exoneration fails.

The rider-requested-detour exoneration in POL-RD-04 fails for want of any instruction. POL-RD-04 requires an instruction recorded in the chat_log, from the rider, timestamped before or within 3 minutes of the vehicle leaving the optimal corridor, and specific enough to act on; the chat export for this trip holds zero messages and is not truncated, so there is no message, no waypoint_hint and no corroboration test to run. A driver's after-the-fact recollection of why he chose a road is not a rider instruction.

The remaining exculpatory routes are closed on the face of the record. POL-RD-05 cannot be run in the driver's favour because no relocation is shown: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null. POL-RD-12 does not apply because vehicle_type is RYDE_PLUS, not RYDE_POOL, so the booked optimal of 5.6 km (not a matched-itinerary figure) is the correct baseline. POL-RD-11 does not displace the arithmetic because fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null. With every adjustment and every alternative regime inapplicable, POL-RD-02 governs the remedy.

Running POL-RD-02 against the booked optimal route: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 5.6 + 0.28 x 9.0) x the surge_multiplier recorded on the fare_breakdown, which is 1.0) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 on-optimal-route ERP + 0.00 waiting_time_fee + 0.00 fixed surcharge - 0.00 promo_discount = 11.32. The refund is charged_total 17.92 less 11.32 = 6.60, which is 36.8% of charged_total, above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, and below the 90% threshold that would convert it to a full refund. On this clause alone the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 6.60.

POL-RD-06's pattern test is met on the citable trailing-window field alone. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 4, which is 3 or more, against 210 completed trips in the same 90-day window and 110 in the last 30 days. I rest the pattern on deviation_flags_90d only: prior_deviation_flags (6) is a lifetime counter, is not the figure POL-RD-06 asks for, and is context only under POL-GEN-01 — I do not substitute it, and it is not needed here.

Because the deviation is both MATERIAL and substantiated on this trip's own evidence — a clean, gap-free trace, a matching trip record and a matching ledger — POL-RD-06(b) licenses FULL_REFUND of charged_total rather than the POL-RD-02 partial, and I ask the tribunal to rule that uplift. As the clause requires, the two figures are stated side by side so the size of the uplift is auditable: the POL-RD-02 figure is SGD 6.60, and the uplifted figure is SGD 17.92. Nothing is carved out by the pass-through carve-out: the fare carries no ERP or toll lines (0.00), no airport surcharge (0.00, and this trip does not originate at an airport), so the whole of the SGD 17.92 charged total is refundable to the rider.

No pass-through correction is owed to the platform here, and none can reduce the figure: the fare_breakdown itemises zero gantries, a zero ERP total and a zero airport surcharge, so POL-RD-09(1)'s anti-double-count rule has nothing to bite on and POL-RD-09(4) identifies no phantom line or wrongly applied surcharge. The refund is therefore not reduced by any pass-through line, and no charge line on the ledger lacks a counterpart in the trace or the trip record.

The rider's complaint that this is not the first time is answered by the record's own route rather than by anything outside it. POL-RD-06(c) refers this driver to driver-conduct review, and that referral is an addition to, not a substitute for, the monetary ruling — the money still moves. I do not ask for refunds on the earlier rides the claim mentions: those trips are not in this evidence bundle, and the sanctioned way to reach the history is the trailing 90-day deviation count under POL-RD-06, which I have cited.

claims.text: This dispute is confined to TRP-00502. The only trip identifier anywhere in the pool is TRP-00502 — trip_record and fare_breakdown agree — and the contested SGD 17.92 is exactly that trip's charged total, with no other fare, receipt or trip record in evidence. The rider's assertion that 'my last three rides' were each longer than the map said, and her demand that somebody 'look at his history', point to no artifact at all: under POL-RD-08 an assertion that cites no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded, and under POL-GEN-01 no profile, history or reputation may ground a finding about this trip.

The trace itself is not in issue: EV-GPS-00502 is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, 100% coverage, 145 fixes, sample interval 10 s against an expected 10 s, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 s, so POL-RD-07 is not engaged and the derived excess of 3.17 km stands as computed. What the driver's case turns on is cause, not measurement. His account on the file is that a road-works sign near Telok Blangah made him take the hill road — an external-event defence of exactly the kind POL-RD-03 exists to test. The artifact that test requires is absent: EV-ADVIS-00502-01 is a MISSING traffic advisory, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, recorded as 'No advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window'. That impairment is disclosed here as POL-GEN-02 requires, and the absence itself is citable: with no advisory there is no named road or junction, no validity window and no shortest lawful alternative distance, so POL-RD-03's conditions cannot be run at all and the driver's defence neither succeeds nor fails on this record.

A closure asserted with no traffic_advisory is the very example POL-RD-10(5) gives of a mandatory escalation trigger, and this is that case: the driver invokes POL-RD-03 against an artifact that is missing from the pool. That escalation is terminal under POL-GEN-03 — it replaces the ruling, no monetary outcome issues, and the SGD 17.92 is held rather than collected or refunded. The same floor is reached through POL-GEN-02: the fact that would resolve the driver's exoneration is carried by an artifact at weight 0.0, so no ruling resting on it can clear the platform's 0.70 confidence floor, which is itself a POL-RD-10(1) trigger. The evidence that would resolve it is the LTA advisory for the optimal corridor in the trip window of 21 Aug 2026, 20:40–21:10 SGT: if it names a road or junction the optimal route uses, the exoneration test can be run; if none exists, the driver's account is simply untestable and a human reviewer should say so.

If the tribunal rules instead of escalating, the remedy is bounded by POL-RD-02's arithmetic and nothing else. On the fare_breakdown the recomputed fare is SGD 11.32 — base 3.80, plus 0.75 x 5.6 km, plus 0.28 x 9 min, plus the 0.80 platform fee, with the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier and nowhere else — against a charged total of SGD 17.92, giving a refund of SGD 6.60 and a payable of SGD 11.32. That is 36.8% of the charge, far below the 90% share below which a full refund is unavailable even on the clause's own arithmetic. The rider's demand for the entire fare back, and for the other rides as well, is not a remedy any clause in this policy provides.

The driver_profile may be consulted because POL-RD-01 records a material deviation, but the clause that permits the consultation also confines it. Even taking its count limb at face value (deviation_flags_90d = 4 against 210 completed trips in 90 days — a ratio of 1.9%, below the same clause's 5% ratio limb), POL-RD-06 states that no pattern may ever establish that this particular trip deviated, and limb (a)'s resolution in the rider's favour is confined to a genuinely balanced record. The only limb that could move money here is limb (b), the deterrent uplift of a POL-RD-02 partial into a full refund; that uplift presupposes a deviation whose cause has been adjudicated, and the only cause on this file is the driver's untested external-event account. That is a reason for escalation, not for a full refund, and it is a reason for the referral under limb (c) at most — a referral that moves no money and displaces no ruling.

No pass-through or billing-integrity correction runs in the rider's favour either. The fare breakdown itemises zero ERP or toll charges (erp_lines total SGD 0.00, erp_gantries empty) and no airport surcharge, and this trip does not originate at an airport, so there is no off-route gantry, no phantom line and no wrongly applied surcharge to refund under POL-RD-09. The only money actually in issue is the distance and time charge that POL-RD-02 governs — which is why the rider's request for the whole fare, and for other rides, has no arithmetic behind it.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. I am sending this case to a human reviewer and making no money ruling: the contested SGD 17.92 is held, not collected and not refunded.

What the trip shows. TRP-00502 was driven 8.77 km (GPS trace EV-GPS-00502, weight 1.0 — 145 fixes, 10 s sampling, 100% coverage, no gaps, so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07) against a booked optimal of 5.6 km (EV-TRIP-00502). The excess is 3.17 km, 56.6% of the optimal route — past both POL-RD-01 gates and past its 50% materiality line. The deviation is therefore established and MATERIAL on this trip's own evidence, and POL-RD-06's driver-profile check is engaged.

Why I cannot decide the money. Driver — your account on the file is that a road-works sign near Telok Blangah made you take the hill road. That is the external-event defence POL-RD-03 governs, and it can only be tested against an LTA traffic advisory naming a road or junction the optimal route uses, with a window covering the time you would have reached it. No such advisory is in the record: EV-ADVIS-00502-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT ('No advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window'). POL-RD-10(5) makes that a mandatory escalation: an exculpatory clause invoked against an artifact absent from the record means the defence cannot be run, and the policy requires a human to resolve it rather than a confident ruling in either direction. I make no finding that you deviated without cause, and none that your account is true.

Rider — the same gap is why I cannot award your refund today, although the arithmetic runs your way. If the deviation stood unexculpated, POL-RD-02 would recompute the fare at ((3.80 + 0.75 × 5.6 + 0.28 × 9.0) × 1.0) + 0.80 = SGD 11.32, giving charged_total 17.92 − recomputed_fare 11.32 = a refund of SGD 6.60 (surge taken from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier = 1.0; no ERP, toll or airport-surcharge lines). And because the deviation is material and the driver's trailing-90-day pattern is established (driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d = 4; I do not use prior_deviation_flags, a lifetime counter that is context only under POL-GEN-01), POL-RD-06(b) would uplift that SGD 6.60 to the full SGD 17.92 if the deviation were substantiated — the two figures the clause requires to be shown side by side. But both figures turn on the deviation surviving the driver's exoneration, which is the very question the record cannot answer, so neither is the ruling.

Your further requests. A refund on your earlier rides is not something any clause here provides: those trips are not in this bundle — no trip identifier, fare breakdown or trace for them is before me — and POL-GEN-01 forbids deciding anything about this trip from a party's history or profile. Your wish that the driver's record be examined is met by the referral below, not by a money award. POL-RD-09 gives nothing to correct: the fare breakdown carries no gantry lines, a zero ERP/toll total and no airport surcharge. POL-RD-04 fails for want of any chat instruction (the chat log for this trip is empty, so no waypoint_hint and nothing to corroborate), POL-RD-05 for want of any amendment, and POL-RD-12 because the vehicle type is RYDE_PLUS, not RYDE_POOL.

Referral (rides with the escalation; it moves no money). POL-RD-06(c): the trailing-90-day pattern being established, driver DRV-20334 is referred to driver-conduct review.

What would resolve this: the LTA traffic advisory for the optimal corridor in the window 21 Aug 2026, 20:40–21:10 SGT. If it names a road or junction the optimal route uses, POL-RD-03 can be run; if no such advisory exists, the driver's account is untestable and a human reviewer should say so.

Confidence is 0.75: the escalation is required on POL-RD-10(5)'s own terms, and the fact the case would otherwise turn on is absent from the record rather than contradicted by it; a MISSING artifact at weight 0.0 carries no fact and neither raises nor lowers that figure.
referrals: POL-RD-06(c): refer driver DRV-20334 to driver-conduct review — the trailing-90-day deviation pattern is established on driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d = 4 (threshold 3).

The trace itself is not in issue: EV-GPS-00502 is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, 100% coverage, 145 fixes, sample interval 10 s against an expected 10 s, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 s, so POL-RD-07 is not engaged and the derived excess of 3.17 km stands as computed. What the driver's case turns on is cause, not measurement. His account on the file is that a road-works sign near Telok Blangah made him take the hill road — an external-event defence of exactly the kind POL-RD-03 exists to test. The artifact that test requires is absent: EV-ADVIS-00502-01 is a MISSING traffic advisory, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, recorded as 'No advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window'. That impairment is disclosed here as POL-GEN-02 requires, and the absence itself is citable: with no advisory there is no named road or junction, no validity window and no shortest lawful alternative distance, so POL-RD-03's conditions cannot be run at all and the driver's defence neither succeeds nor fails on this record.

A closure asserted with no traffic_advisory is the very example POL-RD-10(5) gives of a mandatory escalation trigger, and this is that case: the driver invokes POL-RD-03 against an artifact that is missing from the pool. That escalation is terminal under POL-GEN-03 — it replaces the ruling, no monetary outcome issues, and the SGD 17.92 is held rather than collected or refunded. The same floor is reached through POL-GEN-02: the fact that would resolve the driver's exoneration is carried by an artifact at weight 0.0, so no ruling resting on it can clear the platform's 0.70 confidence floor, which is itself a POL-RD-10(1) trigger. The evidence that would resolve it is the LTA advisory for the optimal corridor in the trip window of 21 Aug 2026, 20:40–21:10 SGT: if it names a road or junction the optimal route uses, the exoneration test can be run; if none exists, the driver's account is simply untestable and a human reviewer should say so.
ledger.detail: the claim cites impaired artifact EV-ADVIS-00502-01 at weight_multiplier 0.0 but does not name its issue code(s): MISSING_ARTIFACT

ledger.claim: If the tribunal rules instead of escalating, the remedy is bounded by POL-RD-02's arithmetic and nothing else. On the fare_breakdown the recomputed fare is SGD 11.32 — base 3.80, plus 0.75 x 5.6 km, plus 0.28 x 9 min, plus the 0.80 platform fee, with the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier and nowhere else — against a charged total of SGD 17.92, giving a refund of SGD 6.60 and a payable of SGD 11.32. That is 36.8% of the charge, far below the 90% share below which a full refund is unavailable even on the clause's own arithmetic. The rider's demand for the entire fare back, and for the other rides as well, is not a remedy any clause in this policy provides.

The driver_profile may be consulted because POL-RD-01 records a material deviation, but the clause that permits the consultation also confines it. Even taking its count limb at face value (deviation_flags_90d = 4 against 210 completed trips in 90 days — a ratio of 1.9%, below the same clause's 5% ratio limb), POL-RD-06 states that no pattern may ever establish that this particular trip deviated, and limb (a)'s resolution in the rider's favour is confined to a genuinely balanced record. The only limb that could move money here is limb (b), the deterrent uplift of a POL-RD-02 partial into a full refund; that uplift presupposes a deviation whose cause has been adjudicated, and the only cause on this file is the driver's untested external-event account. That is a reason for escalation, not for a full refund, and it is a reason for the referral under limb (c) at most — a referral that moves no money and displaces no ruling.

No pass-through or billing-integrity correction runs in the rider's favour either. The fare breakdown itemises zero ERP or toll charges (erp_lines total SGD 0.00, erp_gantries empty) and no airport surcharge, and this trip does not originate at an airport, so there is no off-route gantry, no phantom line and no wrongly applied surcharge to refund under POL-RD-09. The only money actually in issue is the distance and time charge that POL-RD-02 governs — which is why the rider's request for the whole fare, and for other rides, has no arithmetic behind it.
